 Victor Wembanyama had himself a night with 30 points (10-of-18 FGs, 6-of-9 FTs), 14 rebounds, two assists, two blocks, and four 3-pointers in the 124-109 win over the Kings. 
 Wembanyama just took advantage of the Kings defense and got whatever he wanted. What is notable is that he did role his ankle near the end of the first half due to a Sabonis closeout, so it’s possible he shows up on the injury report, but he did finish the game which is good to see. Compared to his stat line last game, this performance seems like a letdown which goes to show how good Wembanyama is.
 -  Brian Taylor

 Victor Wembanyama finished Wednesday’s win over the Mavericks with 52 points (16-of-28 FGs, 19-of-23 FTs), 24 rebounds, two assists, two steals, eight blocks and one three-pointer. 
 The Mavericks aren’t the first team to have no answer for Wembanyama, and they certainly won’t be the last. He was dominant throughout, becoming the second player in league history to finish a game with at least 50 points, 20 rebounds and five blocks since the NBA began recording blocks as an official stat. The other player: Bob McAdoo in 1974. Wembanyama’s 52 points are a new career high, and he shot 1-of-8 from beyond the arc. Just an incredible showing from one of the NBA’s elite talents. Wembanyama appeared to tweak his right ankle in the fourth quarter, but he did not receive medical attention while on the bench and returned for crunch time.

 Wembanyama had a quieter offensive night after scoring at least 29 points in each of his last three games entering play Monday. Still, Wemby filled up the box score other than missing all five of his three-point attempts. The 22-year-old center is still in for a monster week with three more games, starting with a matchup against the Mavericks at home Wednesday.

 Victor Wembanyama tallied 43 points (17-of-34 FGs, 6-of-9 FTs), seven rebounds, four assists, one steal, six blocks and three three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Timberwolves. 
 The Timberwolves didn’t have Rudy Gobert (back) on Saturday, and Wemby took full advantage. The Spurs’ center took a career-high 34 shots, shot 50 percent from the field and finished with the tenth 40-point game of his career. Add in the rebounds and blocks, and this was an excellent end to the week for those rostering Wembanyama. The Spurs play four games next week, starting with the Jazz on Monday.

 Wembanyama took advantage of the mediocre Jazz defense and got whatever he wanted in this game. His defensive presence changes how offenses attack the rim. He has been exactly what you wanted if you drafted him with the first pick in redraft leagues. Its hard to complain and you hope he doesn’t get hurt if you have him.

 Victor Wembanyama finished Tuesday’s win over the Kings with 29 points (14-of-21 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), 10 rebounds, two assists, two steals and five blocks. 
 The Spurs removed the drama from Tuesday’s game in the first half, and Wembanyama dominated the first quarter. In that period, he recorded 17 points, five rebounds, one steal and two blocked shots to help San Antonio build a 10-point lead. Julian Champagnie took over in the second, and because the game was a blowout, Wemby played only 27 minutes. The limited minutes should bode well for Wembanyama’s availability for Wednesday’s game against the Jazz.

 Victor Wembanyama tallied 23 points (9-of-18 FGs, 3-of-5 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, one steal, four blocks and two three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Mavericks. 
 Wembanyama and the Spurs notched their first win of the season on Saturday, rebounding from a tough loss to the Rockets the night prior to defeat the Mavericks in Dallas. He finished with four blocks, bringing his season total to 12. Wemby led the league in blocks last season and won Defensive Player of the Year honors. He’s on track to duplicate those feats in 2026-27. The Spurs play three games in Week 2, starting Tuesday against the Kings.

 Victor Wembanyama had 25 points (9-of-21 FGs, 5-of-8 FTs), 13 rebounds, two assists, two blocks and two three-pointers against the Rockets on Friday. 
 Wembanyama bounced back nicely after going 1-of-13 with 12 points in Tuesday’s loss to the Thunder. The 22-year-old center had 25 points on 9-of-21 shooting, but the Spurs lost again. Amen Thompson blocked Wemby’s shot at point blank range in the final seconds to seal the win for the Rockets. Wembanyama and the Spurs will look to get in the win column against the Mavericks on Saturday.

 Victor Wembanyama posted a double-double on Tuesday with 12 points (1-of-13 FGs, 10-of-12 FTs), 13 rebounds, three assists, one steal and six blocks in a 116-104 loss to the Thunder. 
 Well, this wasn’t how Wemby wanted to start the season. He was able to do enough at the free throw line to get to double figures and record a double-double, but this was an abysmal start to the season for him as a scorer. There is no reason for managers to be worried about this since this will likely be his worst offensive performance of the season. He’ll look to bounce back against the Rockets on Friday.

 The San Antonio Spurs will start DeAaron Fox, Stephon Castle, Dylan Harper, Devin Vassell, and Victor Wembanyama on Friday against the Kings. 
 Jeff McDonald also reported that coach Mitch Johnson intends to use this starting lineup on Tuesday against the Thunder. The Spurs will use their three guard lineup with Champagnie and Harris coming off the bench. We’ll see if the starting lineup sticks that way beyond this upcoming Tuesday, but you can feel good to draft Vassell to stream him in on opening night.

 Wemby may have missed all three of his three-point attempts, but the final stat line was what fantasy managers have come to expect. While a few managers may take Oklahoma City’s Shai Gilgeous-Alexander with pick 1.1, many consider it a two-horse race. If it isn’t Wembanyama going first overall, then it will be Denver’s Nikola Jokić.

 Deni Avdija recorded 22 points (6-of-12 FGs, 9-of-14 FTs), nine rebounds, 11 assists, two steals and one three-pointer in Friday’s loss to the Lakers.
 Avdija shot well from the field and finished one rebound shy of a triple-double. However, he also recorded a season-high eight turnovers. In the Trail Blazers’ last four games, Avdija has dished out 30 assists, taking on even more playmaking responsibilities with Ja Morant (hamstring) sidelined. Also, Friday’s eight turnovers were a departure from the norm, as Deni had not committed more than three in any game this season.

 Lillard led the team in points on Friday, but the production was lacking outside of points and three-pointers.  After falling two rebounds shy of a double-double in Wednesday’s win over the Kings, Kessler recorded his fourth in the Lakers’ last five games on Friday. The 7-footer hasn’t missed a game this season and has already established good chemistry with Lakers stars Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves.  Luka Dončić went off in Friday’s win over the Trail Blazers, finishing with 53 points (17-of-33 FGs, 14-of-18 FTs), five rebounds, five assists, one steal and five three-pointers.
 Dončić finished Friday’s victory with his 11th 50-point game, moving past Kareem Abdul-Jabbar and Allen Iverson to land in tenth on the league’s all-time list. But that wasn’t the only history the Lakers star made on Friday. Dončić has tallied at least 35 points, five rebounds, and five assists in seven straight games, tying Oscar Robertson for the longest such streak in league history. Also, Dončić, who outscored Portland 20-15 in the third quarter, has scored at least 40 points in four straight games. He’s on an incredible run, which is great for those rostering Dončić.
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Acuff didn’t have much of an issue scoring against this Kings defense. His ability as a rookie to take on usage, be relatively efficient, and get buckets and run the offense is impressive.
